title: Move a box to a sensor in Ladder
summary: Start a belt from a button with a set coil and stop it with a reset coil when a box reaches the sensor at the far end.
scope: Tests give deterministic native POSIX host evidence on a simulated plant scene; they are not physical, hardware, HIL, or certification evidence.
objectives: Start an actuator from a button press with a set coil and remember that it is running.
Stop the actuator with a reset coil when a sensor sees the box.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/BeltToSensor.ld.json, keep a Running memory: one rung sets it with Start, a second rung clears it with EyeFar, and two more rungs drive Run and Emit.
stages.checkpoint: Run follows the memory; Emit puts one box on the belt when Start is pressed.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, follow the box: the start button is only a short press, but the belt has to keep running until the box arrives.
stages.checkpoint: Belt off before the press; on after it, with one box on it; off again as soon as EyeFar sees the box, and it stays off.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then run: The starter has no rungs, so the belt never moves; start the belt and put a box on it with Start, and stop the belt when EyeFar sees the box.
stages.checkpoint: The visible scenario must pass with saved host evidence.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: In Tests, choose the saved zplc.json and run only the belt-to-sensor scenario; watch the 3D view while it runs.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named belt-to-sensor and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Watch the box ride the belt in the 3D view and stop under the sensor; compare it with the Run output in the trace.
stages.checkpoint: Run falls when the sensor turns on, not before, and the box is never dropped.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: The EVENTUALLY assertion proves the sensor saw the box within eight seconds; the AT assertions pin the state at the start and at the end.
stages.checkpoint: It does not establish physical belt speed, sensor response, hardware timing, HIL, or certification.

hints.text: Start is a pulse, so the belt needs a memory: a rung with a Start contact and a set coil on Running holds it on, and a rung with an EyeFar contact and a reset coil clears it.
Put the reset rung after the set rung so EyeFar wins when both are TRUE, then add one rung from the Running contact to the Run coil and one from the Start contact to the Emit coil.

faultCases: The starter has no rungs, so the belt never moves; start the belt and put a box on it with Start, and stop the belt when EyeFar sees the box.
